name: g05-01 EBITDA drivers + D&A gap + double net leverage
mechanism: Two separate additions each improved the best EV/EBITDA rule: EBIT margin (the D&A share of EBITDA, i.e. capital consumption) and a heavier weight on net debt to EBITDA (which is an additive part of EV/EBITDA and moves the tax shield and discount rate). The two capture different parts of the multiple, one operating and one financial, so matching both together should align more of what EV/EBITDA prices than either alone.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.306 (no worse than g04-02) and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years.

spec.name: g05-01 EBITDA drivers + D&A gap + double net leverage

name: g05-02 EBITDA drivers + tax and interest leakage
mechanism: Between EBIT and net income sit interest and taxes, which are real cash leaks from EBITDA that a buyer of the whole firm still bears (taxes) or that signal financial risk (interest). Adding net margin next to EBITDA and EBIT margins lines up the full cascade from gross profit to net income, so peers convert EBITDA into after-tax cash flow at similar rates.
prediction: Median error below 0.310 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years.

name: g05-03 EBITDA drivers within 2-digit industry when deep enough
mechanism: Fundamental matching across the whole cross-section beat SIC screens, but firms in the same broad industry also share demand cycles and systematic risk that accounting ratios do not show. Requiring a 2-digit industry match only when it leaves at least 20 candidates, then ranking on the full driver set, adds the shared-cycle information for deep industries and falls back to the cross-section elsewhere.
prediction: Median error below 0.315 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.

name: g05-04 Sales margin match + D&A gap + EV/EBITDA drivers
mechanism: EV/Sales is EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA. Separately, EBIT margin (capital consumption) and the EV/EBITDA drivers capex intensity and net leverage each helped the margin-weighted EV/Sales rule; combining them matches both the margin factor and the EBITDA-multiple factor of the sales multiple at once.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.403 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years.

name: g05-05 Sales margin match + R&D intensity
mechanism: R&D is expensed, so two firms with the same EBITDA margin can differ in how much of their spending is investment in future sales; research-heavy firms deserve more value per dollar of sales. Earlier R&D helped EV/EBITDA but was tested on EV/Sales only without turnover and EBIT margin; adding it to the best sales rule separates investors through opex from firms that are just less profitable.
prediction: Median error below 0.410 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years.

name: g05-06 Sales margin match + net margin cascade
mechanism: Value per dollar of sales depends on the margin left after every claim on cash flow, not only operating costs: EBIT margin removes capital consumption and net margin further removes taxes and interest. Matching net margin next to EBITDA and EBIT margins aligns the after-tax cash yield of each sales dollar and the leverage burden that sits inside EV.
prediction: Median error below 0.408 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years.
